data.name: ConfirmDeletePark

data.comment: Second paragraph of the question before an Indy Park is deleted. {0} is how many structures the park has.

data.name: ConfirmDeleteParkStructuresOther
data.value: Its {0} structures, with their rigs and service modules, its category assignments and its item exceptions are deleted with it. This cannot be undone.

data.name: ConfirmDeleteParkNoStructures
data.value: Its category assignments and its item exceptions are deleted with it. This cannot be undone.

data.name: ConfirmDeleteParkNewDefault

data.name: AutoAssignNothing

data.name: AutoAssignNoMatch

data.name: ConfirmRemoveStructure

data.value: {0} — never seen on contract; counted as 0 ISK

data.value: 1 BPC per run @ ME{0} contract price
data.comment: Production Calculator, Jobs tab, formula column of a blueprint copy line: one copy is bought per run, at its contract price. {0} is the blueprint's material efficiency level (ME).

data.name: SourceIntermediate
data.comment: Production Calculator, Leftovers tab, Source column: left over from an intermediate, a part the plan builds for a later job.

data.name: SourceFinalProduct
data.comment: Production Calculator, Leftovers tab, Source column: left over from a final product, made beyond the quantity asked for.

data.name: SourceBuy
data.comment: Production Calculator, Jobs tab, Source column of a job's material: the plan buys it (a verb, as against "Build").

data.name: SourceBuild
data.comment: Production Calculator, Jobs tab, Source column of a job's material: the plan builds it in a job of its own (a verb, as against "Buy").

data.name: JobModifiers
data.comment: Production Calculator, Jobs tab: what reduces a job's materials. {0} is the blueprint's material efficiency (ME) in percent, {1} the rig bonus, {2} the structure's own bonus, {3} the factor the three make together.

data.name: FormulaMaterial
data.comment: Production Calculator, Jobs tab, formula column: how a material's quantity was worked out. {0} is the quantity per run from the blueprint, {1} the efficiency factor, {2} the runs (twice), {3} the quantity per run after the factor, {4} the result. Keep "ceil" (round up) as it is.
